title: Fill line v1 - the append-only station log grammar
description: One exercised row, as one line of `row-fills.log`. The log is APPEND-ONLY and that is the whole mechanism: a fill is the record of something that was done at a moment, so an edited fill is a claim about the past that nothing can check. This schema describes the PARSED record; the wire format is the line, and `line_grammar` below is the normative regex. Parser: `spec/fill_line.py`. The three properties that make a fill worth anything: it names a CONTRACT value id (not a per-train row label), it carries `tested@<digest>` whenever the finding is about an artifact, and its evidence is verbatim - the words the station recorded, not a summary written later.

line_grammar.$comment: Documentation slot, never present on a parsed record. Kept here so the regex and the schema cannot drift into two files.

ts.description: When the exercise happened, to the second, UTC. Truncated forms (`13:0xZ`) are refused: a fill that cannot be ordered against the PRD's derived_at cannot be shown to be ex-post, and ex-ante/ex-post ordering is the only thing separating a work order from a transcript.

value_id.description: The contract value this fill answers. THE ONLY KEY. A per-train label (A1, F3) names a row that exists for one train and is unverifiable downstream, which is the failure this pattern replaces.

verdict.description: PASS - exercised, claim holds. FAIL - exercised, claim does not hold; the car drops with a comment on the record. PART - exercised, claim holds partly; the evidence says which part and the row does not compile to `proven` without a further PASS or a named waiver. WAIVED - a named human accepted it unproven; the name is in the evidence text and becomes values_proven.waived_by. There is no verdict for `we did not get to it`: an unexercised row simply has no line, and the missing line is what refuses departure.

digest.description: `tested@<digest>` - the artifact this finding was produced against. Mandatory in practice for any claim about a built thing: evidence collected against a digest the candidate does not ship proves nothing about the candidate, and the downstream verifier checks exactly that.

evidence.description: Free text, verbatim, in the words the station recorded the finding in. It travels unchanged into values_proven[].evidence[].what, so a fill written as a summary produces an entry whose evidence is a summary.

source_line.description: 1-based line number in the log the record was parsed from. Set by the parser; the reference a reader follows back.

source_file.description: Path of the log, as committed in the stations ledger. Becomes values_proven[].evidence[].ref.

allOf.$comment: A WAIVED fill must name its human somewhere a reader can find, and the only field it has is the evidence text. The schema cannot check for a person, so this clause states the obligation the compiler enforces: compiling a WAIVED fill into values_proven requires waived_by, and the compiler reads it from here.
